TextEng: "I neeed a drink."
"The people in the keep don't like us being here, but Levio'sa keeps us safe."
"The army had better clear out most of the monsters; I have to get back to work."
"The invaders have made it very difficult for us outsiders. We hate being locked up here in the keep."
"The Floating Huntress once built elaborate traps for exotic creatures; mostly for monsters."
"We respect Levio'sa, our Floating Huntress, for how she has protected our interests."
"I see you have returned, <FirstName>. Welcome back. Is there anything I can do for you?"
"We always welcome your performances."
"Greetings, <FirstName>, I am honored that you have chosen to visit the Silver Lily. I am Garrot Fist, the proprietor. How might I be of assistance?"
"Good luck in the election."
"Questions? I'm not big on answering questions. But, since you are a customer, I will try my best. What do you want to know?"
"Is there anything else I can do for you before I get back to work then?"
"What kind of information?"
His eyes flit around the room, watching the doors carefully. "Did you have other questions?"

"Any time a large group of monsters band together, you need to start wondering what kind of creature that Masked Man must be to be both powerful enough and smart enough to organize them and keep discipline."
"I would recommend you speak to Yenna. She has interesting items. Besides, I think she is interesting to speak to."
"You should speak to Levio뭆a. I think she might have been looking for someone to do a small job for her."
"I try to avoid politics. It would be interesting to see what you would do if you won. I do not appreciate either extreme attitude of your competition. But I would not involve myself in such things."
"Another excellent performance! You are truly a master bard."
"Force of habit, I fear. It is no great secret. I was once an assassin, but I grew sick of my occupation, so I quit. Unfortunately, the people I worked for decided I wasn't allowed to quit."
"When I ran away, they sent hunters after me. It has been a few years since one showed up, but I expect there will be more. These people never quit."
"I thought that traveling all the way north to the borderlands and throwing away my poisoned blade would free me from them, but even here they have followed."
"Not really, just try not to sneak up behind me. I get jumpy about that sort of thing."
"Ah, it has been a long time since I discarded this weapon. Would you mind if I took it back, just as a memento. I can give you something else in return."
"I have a pair of magical boots that I no longer use, if you would take them in trade."
"If that is your will, then so be it. I have no real need of the weapon; it was just a keepsake from the old days. What else would you like?"
"I don't really have anything else of equal value to give you. The boots are quite good, even if they are old."
"That is very kind of you. I am beholden to you, and perhaps someday I shall find a way to pay you back for this. Do you have other questions?"
"Thank you. This might just save my life some day, if the hunters return. I hope you like the boots. Was there anything else?"
"You have been a good customer, and a beacon of hope for us in the keep. I shall only charge you an extra ten gold."
His head jerks around nervously to make certain that none of his other guests can overhear, then he leans in and whispers conspiratorily.
"She wants me to tell you about it? I guess you have a right to know, if anybody does. But take care, this information has cost one person her life already."
"Several years ago, the keep was hit with a storm of the likes not seen in over a century. While the storm raged, a carriage came up to the keep and demanded entrance."
"A dark and frightening footman opened the carriage and a beautiful and elegantly dressed lady stepped out and came into my inn."
"On the contrary, when one beheld her all cares were cast away and troubles became entirely insignificant."
"Her face was enchanting; it drew every eye and held it. She moved with such elegant grace, it was like watching a cat strut across a room like she owned everything."
"She paid for my most expensive room and told me she would be staying for at least a week. When she retired for the night, the only subject of conversation was the mysterious beauty."
"But she never gave me a name. She asked me to simply call her milady. I thought it was odd, but who was I to argue with such beauty... and such gold. She was rich and willing to share."
"The lady stayed in her room for several days, and the storm raged on the entire time. She would order food from the maid that I provided her."
"Patience. I will get there. The lady stayed in her room for several days, and the storm raged on the entire time. She would order food from the maid that I provided her."
"I am sure that when you have enough gold, you will be back. Good day to you."
"I know the serving girl was receiving gold from the lady, but over the course of several days, the girl began to become skittish."
"I asked her what was wrong, but every time she went to speak, the words stuck in her throat."

"Exactly. I became concerned, so I found a way to eavesdrop on the lady's room, from in the attic. At first I could hear chanting and mumbling, but then I noticed that it was just a repetition of a single phrase."
"She was saying, 'Come north, come north, follow the rumors, come north. Hear me <FirstName>. Follow the Masked man. Come to your new home."
"I had never heard your name, so all I knew was that this woman was using magic to call someone."
"Why would I do such a thing. I have nothing against you and nothing to gain from such a lie."
"The lady left shortly thereafter. I neither saw nor heard from her ever again, but I believe that she must have returned, or sent someone here."
"About a month later, the maid was down in the market square, gossiping about the lady, when suddenly she went pale, stopped speaking and walked away."
"Her corpse was found in a back alley, mangled and partially eaten. I wondered if there was a connection, so I went to Yenna, for she is the most powerful person in the keep."
"It was the look on my maid's face. It was the same look that she had when she worked for the lady. My instincts are very sharp when it comes to observing people, and I know it was related."
"It is small enough cost and I need to pay the staff, don't I?"
"I suspect that you shall discover more as you get to know the residents of the keep. But whatever this person is, be very careful. She obviously has some power over your mind."
"Good luck, <FirstName>. I hope you can overcome your adversaries and live a long life."
"Never. I would tell no one, for even if they believed me, what could anyone else do? Yenna is very powerful. I knew she would grasp the connection better than anyone."
"What could he do? I was every bit as capable as him and Yenna was stronger than us both."
"Obviously. Yenna contacted me and told me not to tell anyone, unless she sent them to me. I suspect that there is someone living in the keep who knows this lady."
"And so we came north at your insistence, though none of the rest of us ever heard these rumors. What can this mean?"
"This does explain your single-minded drive to hunt such a powerful creature, <FirstName>."
"That is why you chased the Masked Man even when Trip gives you sensible advice, <FirstName>! You had a voice in your head, just like me!"
"<FirstName>, that is why you kept pressing us to chase down the Masked Man, even when we tried to argue with you."
"We only have a few rooms left, though they are nice ones. It costs 30 gold per week, and I will take the first 30 right up front."
"Do not give it another thought. I am proud to say you stayed here at the Silver Lily."
" With all the landowners forced to stay in the keep, business has been plentiful. Are you interested?"
"If you should change your mind, I would be more than happy to offer you a room. Was there anything else you needed?"

"I can do no such thing, I fear. My establishment has a certain reputation, and I fear your reputation is not so high that I can ignore profits. 30 gold is a fair price for the higher quality services I provide."
"I cannot go that low and continue to keep the quality of service and clientele that raise my establishment over the likes of the Mossy Tree. I will go as low as 25, but that is my best offer."
"Well, you do look fairly respectable, and on the slight chance you might win the election, perhaps you will remember my kindness. 20 gold it is."
"That certainly has merit. I have been looking for a good bard. So are you any good?"
<StartCheck>[Success]</Start> "Wonderful. I know you cannot perform all the time, but if you could whenever you come in to rest, I would be happy to have you stay here."
"I will have the room unlocked for you. Was there anything else?"
"Some are paying more. I made an exception for you, because you are something of a celebrity right now."
"Very good. I hope you enjoy your stay here. If you have any questions, just come and speak to me."
"Thank you very much, <FirstName>. I hope you enjoyed your stay here at the Silver Lily."
"Good day, <Lord/Lady> <FirstName>. I hope all is well with you. I must get back to my patrons now. If you will excuse me."
"I saw them enter town and thought I should find out what they were up to. I am glad I could assist you. Now I am no longer beholden to you. I must return to the Silver Lily. Be careful out here."
"You already settled your account. No need to worry about that now."
The innkeeper of the Silver Lily walks around the room with a smooth gait, nervously twitching whenever there is a sudden or strange sound.
"I will perform again for you."
<StartCheck>[Perform]</Start>
"I have some questions to ask you."

"Let's talk about something else."
"What do you know about the Masked Man's forces?"
"Where can I get equipment?"
"Where can I find employment?"
"What do you think of the election?"
"Why are you so nervous?"
"I am here to settle my account."
"Is there anything I can do?"
"You were an assassin? Is this your blade?"
"I think I'll keep the dagger."
"I want more than just an old pair of boots."
"They'll have to do then."
"I don't need anything in return. The dagger was yours."
"That would be good."
"I can't pay it."
"Yenna told me to come and speak to you."
"Did she frighten you also?"
"Who was she?"
"Please, continue."
"Hurry up and get to the important part."
"What has this got to do with me?"
"Like with Yenna?"
"You must be making this up!"
"If you really feel that way, shouldn't the room be free?"
"Did you hear anything else?"
"What happened to the lady?"
"Why do you think it was connected?"
"Thank you for the information."
"Did you tell anyone else?"
"Why didn't you go to the Banner?"
"Thank you."
"And something happened to silence Yenna?"
"I am looking for a room."
"Never mind."
"I'll give you 20 gold."
"I'll take it."
"Here you go."
"I'll take it."
"I'm a bard, could we do an exchange of services?"
<StartCheck>[Perform]</Start> "I'll show you."
"People are actually paying those prices?"
"I'll take it."
"Goodbye."
"Welcome back. How can I help you?" Gelani turns her moon-eyed face to you slowly. She seems preoccupied with some thought or memory, but smiles softly at you all the same.
"What are we doing back here? I have no patience for this, <FirstName>."
"I feel disquieted right now. Probably because of the election, not that I'm involved in politics anymore. Please, ask someone else your questions."
"My name is Gelani and I am part owner of this establishment, along with Mr. Mossy. I was also something more than that once, but those days are gone."
"Sorry, I don't mean to be melancholy, but with the election happening, I long for the days when I was more involved in politics."
"I am always happy to speak to a customer."
"It isn't so dry when exciting things like the election and the Masked Man's invasion are going on. Right now is the most critical moment for a politician, and I have to miss out on it."

"Not so long ago, I was the master of the merchants' guild, a position I really loved. Unfortunately my leadership was usurped by Thaddeus Squilt, a notorious villain with a black heart, but a cunning mind."
"Thaddeus spread rumors about me, and the rumors were backed by a certain noble who, even now, makes a bid for leadership of this dear keep."
"That is like saying a dragon is a little dangerous. It's a gross understatement if I've ever heard one."
"Ask anyone with moral character in town and they will tell you that Thaddeus Squilt is completely untrustworthy. The rumors he started destroyed me."
"He may be more cunning, but he is hardly smarter. He is a terrible, foolish leader. His rumors destroyed my reputation, but he shall destroy the keep."
"What? Murder! Help me!"
"Because I had supported some necessary tax increases in the past, Thaddeus persuaded others that I was planning on supporting a doubling in taxes; which I would never do."
"Unfortunately, with Sir Becket's help, Thaddeus's lies were believed and he became the new guildmaster. Now the entire keep is paying for his poor leadership."
"You think so? We barely survived the Masked Man's attack on the keep... the Banner did not. Part of the blame for his death lies with Thaddeus."
"Ever since Thaddeus stole my position, he has moved to block any increase in taxes. The only reason I ever supported the tax increases was so the Banner could afford to train and arm new guards."
"Now the guards are ill-equipped, inexperienced and demoralized. I do not envy the next Lord or Lady of the Keep."

"Sir Becket is like some evil demon come to us in man-flesh to lead us to our dooms. Every move he makes seems to lead us closer to chaos, rather than to a stable government where trade can flourish."
"Enivid is young and ignorant of political necessities. If she becomes the Lady of the Keep, she will quickly become frustrated with the authority of the guilds."
"Are these the only choices we have? A monster of chaos or an authoritative purist?"
"What matter would you like to speak on?"
"And you think you can be that leader, I suppose? Well, I am in no position to help or hinder you, so I guess it matters not. Still, I was hoping for better from you."

"Greetings, friend, and welcome to the Mossy Tree. If you need anything you should speak to Mr. Mossy." This halfling sips a glass of wine pausing occasionally to stare mournfully into its ruby depths.
"I knew who you were when you came in, but I didn't want to say anything.  But let us speak on some other topic. With no clout in the political realm, there is little point in discussing it with me."
"Really? I knew who you were when you came in, but I didn't want to say anything. I see no reason not to believe you either, since I am in no position to help you."
"I have been talking to some of the other merchants. Some of them are realizing what happened and sympathize with me. Still, it really hurt last time; I don't think I could do it again."
"Very well. What did you want to discuss?"
"Come with you? Where? Why?"
Gelani raises an eyebrow at you and shakes her head. "I don't know what to do. Some of the others are pretty unhappy with the current situation."
"I guess I can. What choice do I have? Fine, let's go now."
"Why should I take such a chance? I need neither the ridicule nor the pain of losing again."
"I know. That is why I sit here and drink. Now, if you will excuse me..."
<StartCheck>[Failure]</Start> "How dare you speak to me that way! I tried, I truly did, but the others voted me out. I will do no such thing ever again!"

"Thank you for the confidence, <FirstName>. I will go and gather the merchants for another vote. Hopefully, by tomorrow, I will be back in power."
"Come and see me in the merchants' guild office, later."
"It is best to stay hidden in shadows, pretty halfling. Leaders find trouble; <FirstName> needs to learn this lesson!"
"People react to threats in different ways. Perhaps with the threat of invasion, the other merchants might listen to another voice?"
"Thaddeus sounds like the kind of person who would do anything to gain power, no matter how despicable the deed. You need to stand against him, no matter how hard!"
"What is wrong? Why do you need me? Where are we going?"
"If this Thaddeus is as corrupt as you say he is, and I believe you speak the truth, do you not owe it to your guild to try to stop him?"
"You have given me much hope for the future, <FirstName>. You will have my vote in the election." Gelani offers you a formal bow, already seeming to consider you her Lord.
"The future looks bright, <Lord/Lady> <FirstName>. Best of luck."
"You scared me for a moment."
"Then I will come immediately."
"Then we should take assistance. Guards, come with us!"
"Then I will follow you, but I shall take some protection. Guards... with me."
"You need to take back your guild!"

The smith works at a fevered pace, whenever customers leave him alone. He nods at you as you approach.
"I really need to get me a front man t'sell the goods so as I can work. Are ye here for me goods or are you gonna waste me time yappin' like a young pup?"
"T'is all fine craftsmanship, bein' me own, so ye can expect the best."
"Back t'work for me. You should consider workin' too, instead of wastin' me time."
"Don't waste me time with stupid questions. I got too much work for inane chatter, so be quick."
"Good, I was sick of yer inane chatter anyways. Now what do ye want?"
"I be thinkin' ye came in here t'waste me time and I'd be preferin' it if ye stuck t'important matters like me work."
"I've got no time for that. Ask someone who spends more than a few minutes a day outside his workshop."
"Well, I have a spare forge over there ye can use if ye have any ability. Just stay out of me way while I work."
"It be on account of me one glass eye. I be surprised ye didn't notice. I don't like talkin' about how I lost it, so don't go askin'."
"T'is all fine craftsmanship, bein' me own, so ye can expect the best, and at a generous cost, since ye be a member of the military guild."
"Goodbye."
"I have some questions for you."
"That's all my questions."
"What do you think of the election?"
"I have questions about the keep."
"I would like to use your forge for my crafting."
"Why is your name Glassy?"
"I would like to see your goods."

You hear muffled sounds coming from a crack in the wall, behind the grate. Although the crack is too low to the ground to see anything through, you might be able to listen if you get closer.
<StartCheck>[Success]</Start> Your fingers grasp a small ring and pull it out. It looks as if it is Sir Becket's signet ring.
There doesn't appear to be anything unusual about this grate.

"That was... satisfactory. Meet me again tonight, after I am finished with Ellysia." The man's voice is unmistakably that of Sir Becket. Just as unmistakeable is the fact that the woman he is speaking to is not his so-called love, Lady Ellysia.
"I think my mistress would be most displeased if she discovered our... relationship."
"I do not pay you to think, and if you ever say a word to Ellysia, I *will* have you killed. No one will care about the death of a lady's maid. Do you understand?"
"Y.. yes, sir."
"Tonight... and bring a friend." The woman leaves.

"Now where's my ring? Well, I'll find it later. I need to find out what this new contender of mine is doing. When it comes to politics, never trust the enemy, they say... I might have to take... steps."
Footsteps fade away as Sir Becket leaves. A flash of light glints off of something gold on the floor right below the crack in the wall.

TextEng: "Secondly, after much thought, I would like to offer the position of Banner to my formidable opponent, <FirstName>. Do you accept?"
Text: "둘째, 숙고 끝에, 기수장 자리를 존경할 만한 상대인 <FirstName>에게 제안하고 싶소. 받아들이겠소?"

TextEng: "Then I find you in contempt of the true ruler of the keep and you are exiled henceforth. Never return on pain of death!"
Text: "그렇다면 거점의 정당한 통치자를 모독한 것이오, 이제부터 추방이오. 목숨이 아까우면 다시는 돌아오지 마시오!"

TextEng: "Very good, and you shall receive lands and pay worthy of such a position, as soon as you complete your first duty."
Text: "좋소, 첫 번째 임무를 완수하는 즉시, 그 직위에 합당한 영지와 보수를 받게 될 것이오."

TextEng: "You have proven to us that you are very capable at warfare, without the aid of inexperienced and weaker troops. This is good, as the military assures us that the troops are needed here in the keep."
Text: "미숙하고 약한 병사의 도움 없이도 전투에 매우 유능하다는 것을 증명했소. 군부가 병력이 거점에 필요하다고 하니 좋은 일이오."

TextEng: "Therefore, for the safety of the keep, you shall go out and destroy the last of the invaders. Do not return to the keep until you are finished. Good luck."
Text: "그러므로 거점의 안전을 위해, 나가서 남은 침략자를 처치하시오. 끝날 때까지 거점에 돌아오지 마시오. 행운을 비오."

TextEng: "The new Lady of the Keep is Enivid."
Text: "거점의 새 영주는 에니비드입니다."

TextEng: "It is my sacred duty to announce that I am calling <FirstName> to be my new Banner. <He/She> has proven <his/her> worth. There is one thing that I ask though."
Text: "신성한 의무로서 <FirstName>을 새 기수장으로 임명한다고 발표합니다. 가치를 증명했습니다. 하지만 한 가지 부탁이 있습니다."

TextEng: "Rooms, I suspect. Unless someone went and knocked out all the walls. Maybe you should go and check. Take a mop and a bucket with you and clean the floors while you뭨e at it."
Text: "방이 있을 걸, 누가 벽을 다 때려부수지 않았다면 말이야. 가서 확인해 봐. 대걸레랑 양동이 들고 가서 바닥이나 닦으면서."

TextEng: "You have proven your abilities in the battlefield. To accept the role as Banner, I ask you to go forth and destroy the last of the invaders."
Text: "전장에서 능력을 증명했습니다. 기수장 역할을 맡으려면, 나가서 남은 침략자를 처치해 주십시오."

TextEng: "When this is done, you may return to the keep, where you will be welcomed with all honors, lands and wealth as deserving of both a hero and a Banner."
Text: "끝나면 거점으로 돌아올 수 있으며, 영웅이자 기수장에 합당한 모든 명예, 영지, 재산으로 환영받을 것입니다."

TextEng: "Then I cannot accept you as my Banner, nor can I allow the divisiveness that your presence might incur. For your assistance, here is 1000 gold, from my own coffers."
Text: "그렇다면 기수장으로 받아들일 수 없으며, 당신의 존재가 야기할 수 있는 분열도 허용할 수 없습니다. 도움에 대한 감사로, 제 금고에서 금화 1000닢을 드립니다."

TextEng: "You are hereby exiled from the keep, never to return. Goodbye, <FirstName>. I am sorry things had to end this way."
Text: "이에 거점에서 추방하며, 다시는 돌아올 수 없습니다. 안녕히, <FirstName>. 이런 식으로 끝나게 되어 유감입니다."

TextEng: "If anyone wishes to go with you, they are welcome to, but the keep has precious few defenders left. Should another enemy strike, the keep would fall."
Text: "함께 가고 싶은 자는 환영하지만, 거점에 남은 방어자가 거의 없습니다. 다른 적이 공격하면, 거점은 함락될 것입니다."

TextEng: "Then take your stalwart companions and go forth to rid our land of this pestilence that festers in our caves."
Text: "그럼 든든한 동료들을 데리고 나가서, 동굴에서 곪아가는 이 역병을 우리 땅에서 몰아내."

TextEng: "Then no one will follow my Banner? I am saddened by this, but I fear this is the way of life."
Text: "아무도 내 기수장을 따르지 않겠다고? 슬프지만, 삶이란 그런 거겠지."

TextEng: "You know I shall never fail you, <FirstName>. We shall slay all who cross us!"
Text: "절대 실망시키지 않을 거라는 걸 알죠, <FirstName>. 방해하는 자는 모조리 처치할 거예요!"

TextEng: "There be no place for Trip, if <FirstName> is not there. Even if it costs my life, Trip is your faithful companion."
Text: "<FirstName>이 없는 곳에 트립의 자리는 없어요. 목숨이 들더라도, 트립은 당신의 충실한 동료예요."

TextEng: "I do not fear death. I am with you."
Text: "죽음이 두렵지 않아요. 함께 가겠어요."

TextEng: "What do I care? Everyone thinks this damn election is so important, but I tell you, life goes on. You think you're all-fired important one minute, then *WHACK* Mistress Death knocks your skull in."
Text: "내가 알 바야? 다들 이 빌어먹을 선거가 그렇게 중요한 줄 알지만, 삶은 계속돼. 잠깐 대단한 척하면, *퍽!* 죽음의 여주인이 머통을 깨버리는 거야."

TextEng: "I will go with ye, as always, <lad/lass>."
Text: "언제나처럼 함께 가겠어요, 친구."

TextEng: "Good luck and may Jaess watch over you, <FirstName>."
Text: "행운을 빕니다, 재스가 지켜보시길, <FirstName>."

TextEng: "My first duty, as Lady of the Keep, is to announce that I am placing Sir Becket under arrest for the attempted murder of <FirstName>."
Text: "거점의 영주로서 첫 번째 직무로, 베켓 경을 <FirstName>의 살인 미수 혐의로 체포할 것을 발표합니다."

TextEng: "You can't do that! I'll get you Enivid, and you too <FirstName>! I have friends!"
Text: "그럴 수 없소! 에니비드, 네 꼴을 보여주겠소, <FirstName>, 너도 마찬가지요! 나한테 동지가 있소!"

TextEng: You're suddenly deafened by a booming screech in your eardrums. Time seems to grind to a halt as a familiar nimbus of light surrounds you. The booming screech resolves into an angry tirade coming from your magic weapon...
Text: 갑자기 귓속이 굉음으로 멍해집니다. 익숙한 빛의 후광이 당신을 감싸며 시간이 멈춘 듯합니다. 굉음은 마법 무기에서 나오는 성난 독설로 바뀝니다...

TextEng: "Foolish child! You have no idea how much your grandmother and I have invested in you! How much we've done, only to see you fail at such a simple task! I guess your grandmother was right about you, <FirstName>... You always were the weaker one."
Text: "어리석은 아이! 네 할머니와 내가 너에게 얼마나 투자했는지 짐작도 못 하겠지! 이토록 간단한 일에서 실패하는 꼴을 보려고 얼마나 노력했는데! 네 할머니 말이 맞았소, <FirstName>... 넌 항상 약한 쪽이었어."

TextEng: "And what have you got to show for all your years of effort and toil, a bad back, poor eyesight and goiter the size of a mace head! So you can keep your election and stuff it up your... shirt."
Text: "그 오랜 세월 노력하고 힘쓴 대가가 뭐야, 아픈 등, 나쁜 시력, 철퇴 머리만 한 혹! 그러니 선거 같은 건 네 옷... 속에나 쑤셔 넣어."

TextEng: "Well now, the Guildmasters can huff and puff and delay all they want but, when it comes right down to it, I suppose I can call it whenever I darn well please, can't I..."
Text: "글쎄, 길드장들이 아무리 훅훅 불고 미루고 해봤자, 결국은 내가 원할 때 시작할 수 있지, 안 그래..."

TextEng: "The only thing I can't do is stop it once I've started. None of those recount shenanigans, understand? If you lose, you lose; no sense in crying over it. So what do you say? Would you like me to call it?"
Text: "시작하면 멈출 수 없다는 거, 그것만 못 해. 재검표 같은 장난은 없어, 알겠지? 지면 진 거야, 울어봤자 소용없어. 어때? 선거를 시작할까?"

TextEng: "It's all the same to me. Now was there something else you wanted? I honestly can't remember."
Text: "나한텐 마찬가지야. 다른 거 원하는 게 있었나? 솔직히 기억이 안 나."

TextEng: "Up and at 'em, everyone! We're having us an election. Why? Because I say so, that's why, you little whippersnappers! All right, <FullName>, I'll go gather the votes and tally the results. Don't make me regret this."
Text: "일어나라, 다들! 선거를 한다. 왜냐고? 내가 한다니까 하는 거야, 이 풋내기들아! 좋아, <FullName>, 가서 투표를 모아 결과를 집계하겠어. 후회하게 만들지 마."

TextEng: "I make sure everything in the keep runs smoothly, from the servants up to the guild masters, all fall within my responsibility."
Text: "거점의 모든 것이 잘 돌아가게 하는 게 내 일이야, 하인부터 길드장까지, 전부 내 책임이야."

TextEng: "When there is a guild vote, I tally the votes. When a servant retires, I hire a new one."
Text: "길드 투표가 있으면 표를 세고, 하인이 은퇴하면 새로 뽑아."

TextEng: "Even if you were, and I know damn well you are not, I'm too old to go bowing down to any <lord/lady>. I am the castellan, so it is my business to know everything that happens in the Guildhall."
Text: "그렇다 해도, 분명 아닌 거 뻔히 아는데, 난 어떤 영주한테든 절하기엔 너무 늙었어. 내가 성주관이니까, 길드 홀에서 일어나는 모든 일은 내 관할이야."

TextEng: "I'll forget you said that."
Text: "그 말은 잊어주지."

TextEng: "No seriously... my mind isn't what it used to be. I will forget you said anything, so there is no point in bribing me, cause when it comes time for the vote, I won't remember what I was supposed to do."
Text: "아니 진짜로... 머리가 예전 같지 않아. 네가 뭘 말했는지 잊어버릴 거니까, 나한테 뇌물을 쓸 필요가 없어, 투표 때가 되면 뭘 해야 했는지 기억도 안 날 테니까."

TextEng: "All I do is count the votes. You can give me all the gold you like, but it won't do you a lick of good."
Text: "난 그냥 표를 세는 거야. 금을 아무리 줘봤자, 1도 도움이 안 돼."

TextEng: "The guilds have voted. I have tallied the votes and here are the results."
Text: "길드들이 투표했습니다. 표를 집계했고 결과는 다음과 같습니다."

TextEng: "<CUSTOM6002> votes for Sir Becket."
Text: "<CUSTOM6002>은 베켓 경에게 투표했습니다."

TextEng: "<CUSTOM6001> votes for Enivid."
Text: "<CUSTOM6001>은 에니비드에게 투표했습니다."

TextEng: "<CUSTOM6003> votes for <FirstName>."
Text: "<CUSTOM6003>은 <FirstName>에게 투표했습니다."

TextEng: "Why do politicians never make up their minds? A three way tie! Now, where did I put that law book on elections... ah ha! Here it is!"
Text: "정치인들은 왜 결정을 못 하나? 3자 동점이야! 자, 선거법 책을 어디 뒀더라... 아하! 여기 있다!"

TextEng: "In case of a tie, the castellan will cast the final and deciding vote. What?!? Like I want to make *that* decision! Dang it all, I will just flip a coin!"
Text: "동점일 경우, 성주관이 최종 결정 투표를 한다. 뭐?!? 내가 *그런* 결정을 하고 싶을 것 같아? 빌어먹을, 동전이나 던지겠어!"

TextEng: "Oh, um... I guess that doesn't really work with three of you."
Text: "아, 음... 셋이면 그건 안 되겠구나."

TextEng: "This is my business, you impertinent upstart. I am the castellan and everything that happens within the Guildhall is my business."
Text: "내 일이라고, 이 건방진 풋내기야. 내가 성주관이고, 길드 홀 안에서 일어나는 모든 일은 내 관할이야."

TextEng: "Do you have a three-sided coin, Mykes?"
Text: "세 면짜리 동전은 없나요, 마이크스?"

TextEng: "There is a very simple solution to that... Sir Becket has always been very rude to me, treating me like an overrated slave."
Text: "아주 간단한 해결책이 있어... 베켓 경은 항상 나한테 무례했거든, 과대평가된 노예 취급을 했어."

TextEng: "Come now, Mykes, it was all in good fun! Right?"
Text: "이봐요, 마이크스, 다 장난이었잖소! 그렇지?"

TextEng: "You are out of the running, which leaves me with just <FirstName> and Enivid to worry about. Hmm, I think I will just flip a coin."
Text: "넌 탈락이야, 그러면 <FirstName>하고 에니비드만 남았네. 흠, 그냥 동전을 던져야겠어."

TextEng: He looks at each of the candidates with a challenging gaze. "And nobody gets to challenge this decision!"
Text: 그가 도전적인 눈빛으로 각 후보를 바라봅니다. "그리고 아무도 이 결정에 이의를 제기하지 못해!"

TextEng: "What? You cannot just flip a coin! Just choose me, you imbecilic, senile... er... Mikey, old chap. Please?"
Text: "뭐라고? 동전을 던지다니! 그냥 날 선택하시오, 이 백치, 노망... 에... 마이키, 친구. 부탁이오."

TextEng: "No, the texts are quite clear! I get the final vote, and since I could really care less who gets the job, I will flip a coin. Heads, <FirstName>. Tails, Enivid. Now where did I place my coin purse... "
Text: "아니, 법전에 분명히 나와 있어! 최종 투표는 내 몫이고, 누가 되든 1도 상관 안 하니까, 동전을 던지겠어. 앞면, <FirstName>. 뒷면, 에니비드. 자, 동전 지갑을 어디 뒀더라..."

TextEng: "Why do politicians never make up their minds? It would appear we have a tie between Becket and Enivid. Now, where did I put that law book on elections... ah ha! Here it is!"
Text: "정치인들은 왜 결정을 못 하나? 베켓과 에니비드가 동점인 것 같군. 자, 선거법 책을 어디 뒀더라... 아하! 여기 있다!"

TextEng: "Why do politicians never make up their minds? It would appear we have a tie between Enivid and <FirstName>. Now, where did I put that law book on elections... ah ha! Here it is!"
Text: "정치인들은 왜 결정을 못 하나? 에니비드와 <FirstName>이 동점인 것 같군. 자, 선거법 책을 어디 뒀더라... 아하! 여기 있다!"

TextEng: "Why do politicians never make up their minds? It would appear we have a tie between Becket and <FirstName>. Now, where did I put that law book on elections... ah ha! Here it is!"
Text: "정치인들은 왜 결정을 못 하나? 베켓과 <FirstName>이 동점인 것 같군. 자, 선거법 책을 어디 뒀더라... 아하! 여기 있다!"

TextEng: He grunts and nods his head. "I guess I've heard of you. If you have any questions about the keep... figure it out yourself."
Text: 그가 투덜거리며 고개를 끄덕입니다. "들어는 봤어. 거점에 대해 궁금한 게 있으면... 알아서 해."

Text: "아니, 법전에 분명히 나와 있어! 최종 투표는 내 몫이고, 누가 되든 1도 상관 안 하니까, 동전을 던지겠어. 앞면, <FirstName>. 뒷면, 에니비드. 자, 동전 지갑을 어디 뒀더라..."
